label: Vireo Valley: repeated cleaned_or_serviced on module with declining benefit
headline: The Vireo Valley 'wash benefit collapsing from 8% to 2%' signal is two hand-typed estimates on two different blocks with templated narratives and miscoded resolution codes — no action warranted beyond fixing how wash outcomes are recorded.
action: Close this candidate and instead require wash work orders at Vireo Valley to record pre/post soiling-ratio or SCADA-derived MWh with the correct CLEANED resolution code, so wash efficacy can be tested on real repeat-block data next season.
reasoning: The entire 8%-to-2% 'decay' rests on exactly two numeric observations: WO-2025-00748 (B01, 8%, TECH-0229) and WO-2026-00467 (B07, 2%, TECH-0051). The other three members (WO-2025-00280, WO-2025-00982, WO-2025-00997) carry benefit_pct=null and two of them are 'not_applicable' outcomes, so there is no repeated service of a single block with a declining recovery — the required same-block, same-interval comparison called out as H3's discriminating evidence simply does not exist in this data. H2 is plausible in direction (the 8% wash followed heavy ag-dust on B01 per WO-2025-00280, while B07 in May 2026 has no comparable loading narrative) but it also cannot be tested with one point per period. Controls reinforce H1/H4: WO-2025-01007 at Caprock Mesa and WO-2026-00222 at Coralito Flats are near-verbatim copies of the Vireo 'finished ahead of the wind advisory' text, showing the wash write-ups are templated boilerplate rather than measured observations, and neither carries a benefit figure either. Add the miscoded resolution codes on module washes (SW-UPDATE on WO-2025-00748, RESET on WO-2026-00467) and no lost_mwh corroboration anywhere, and this is a reporting/small-sample artifact, not a physical loss mechanism.
contradicting: The two quantified washes do differ by 6 points in the direction of decay, and Vireo Valley does show module-adjacent activity at the site (WO-2025-00378 is an inverter ground fault, not module degradation, so it is weak support at best). If future washes at Vireo Valley continue to report low single-digit benefit after long dry intervals with heavy dust narratives, H3 would regain standing.

population_detail.description: No defensible at-risk module population; only two blocks (B01, B07) carry any benefit figure and neither was washed twice within the window.

hypotheses.statement: The apparent efficacy decay is a small-sample data artifact: only 2 of the 5 work orders carry a numeric benefit_pct, so 'early 8% vs late 2%' is a comparison of two single observations across four different blocks (B01, B03, B05, B07) rather than repeated service of one degrading asset.
predictions: Exactly two member work orders have non-null benefit_pct; the other three have benefit_pct=null and outcome 'not_applicable' or unquantified 'resolved'.
The asset_id field is blank or different on every member work order, so no single module block is washed more than once within the cluster window.
Other sites/components with the same wash action show benefit_pct spreads of comparable magnitude (2-10%) with no time trend, i.e. a 6-point gap is inside normal scatter.
lost_mwh_reported_total = 0 for all members, meaning no independent production evidence supports any efficacy claim.
Bootstrapping or re-binning the cluster (e.g. splitting at a different date) flips or erases the 'decline'.
discriminating_evidence: Count of non-null benefit_pct values in the cluster: if <3 per period, no decay trend is statistically supportable.
Whether any single asset_id appears twice with declining benefit; that would defeat this hypothesis and support H3.
Site-wide distribution of wash benefit_pct across all Vireo Valley washes (not just the 5 members) plotted against date.

hypotheses.statement: Benefit per wash varies with how much soiling had accumulated before the wash, not with module health: the 8% wash followed a heavy ag-dust loading event while the 2% wash followed a period of lighter/washed-off soiling, so the 'decline' is ordinary seasonal and cadence-driven variation.
predictions: Days-since-previous-wash for the same block is substantially shorter before the low-benefit (2%) wash than before the high-benefit (8%) wash.
Work orders with environment tag 'dust_or_soiling' and symptom 'soiling' show higher benefit_pct than those tagged 'routine_service'/'none_mentioned', regardless of date.
Total wash frequency at Vireo Valley increases over the span (more PM wash WOs per quarter in 2026 than 2025), consistent with diminishing marginal benefit per event.
Narratives around the low-benefit wash mention rain, wind, or light dust rather than heavy accumulation.
discriminating_evidence: Correlation between benefit_pct and days-since-last-wash on the same block: strong positive correlation supports this over H3.
If benefit_pct stays low even after a long dry interval with heavy dust narratives, this hypothesis fails and H3 gains.
Seasonal alignment: whether low-benefit washes cluster in post-wet-season months across multiple years.

hypotheses.statement: Vireo Valley modules in the washed blocks have developed an irreversible loss mechanism (cemented/abrasive soiling, AR-coating or glass degradation) such that cleaning recovers progressively less output at equal pre-wash soiling levels.
predictions: Later washes at Vireo Valley show lower benefit_pct than earlier ones even after controlling for days-since-last-wash and soiling symptom tag.
Vireo Valley wash benefit trends downward while other sites' wash benefit stays flat over the same window.
Increasing counts of non-wash module work orders at Vireo Valley (inspection, underperformance, hotspot, string-current-low) accompanying or following the low-benefit washes.
Repeat washes of the same block within a short interval, or escalation from CLEANED to replacement/warranty resolution codes on module assets.
discriminating_evidence: A same-block, same-season, same-interval pair of washes with declining benefit — the only observation that isolates module condition from soiling load.
Presence or absence of module-level underperformance work orders at Vireo Valley that are independent of washing.
Cross-site comparison: if the benefit decline is site-specific and survives covariate control, H3 is favoured over H1/H2.

hypotheses.statement: The benefit numbers are informal tech estimates whose reporting convention drifted (rounded SCADA eyeballing, template copy-paste, one dominant tech), so the 8%-to-2% change reflects who wrote the note rather than any physical change.
predictions: Numeric benefit_pct appears almost exclusively in narratives containing the phrase pattern 'Output up about N percent on the next clear day per SCADA'; other wash WOs omit it entirely.
Benefit values are heavily quantised (round integers like 2, 5, 8, 10) with no fractional values anywhere in the corpus.
Near-duplicate narrative text appears across work orders (e.g. the two 'finished ahead of the wind advisory' notes three days apart), indicating templated write-ups.
Resolution codes are inconsistent with the described work (SW-UPDATE and RESET recorded for module washes), showing loose coding discipline at this site.
Benefit_pct distribution differs systematically by tech_id even for similar jobs.
discriminating_evidence: Group benefit_pct by tech: if TECH-0229 (the 8%) and TECH-0051 (the 2%) differ consistently across all their work orders, reporting style explains the gap.
Rate of resolution-code/action mismatches at Vireo Valley vs other sites.
Whether any independent production or lost-MWh field corroborates the stated percentages; total lost_mwh_reported = 0 suggests it does not.
